newsitem.title: UK: EMS/MARK SETTLES AT PEAKS AFTER JUMP IN EUROPE.
newsitem.headline: EMS/MARK SETTLES AT PEAKS AFTER JUMP IN EUROPE.

text.p: The mark settled at peaks against its European crosses at midday after racing higher as the Bundesbank warned the pace of German inflation had picked up and it would steer policy to ensure price stability is maintained.
Currency traders and analysts said mark strength in Europe reflected perceptions that rates in Germany could be heading up.

The mark pushed to seven-day highs of 3.3744 French francs and 979.50 Italian lire. Against the Spanish peseta, the German unit jumped to 6-1/2 week highs of 84.58 pesetas. Against its Nordic satellites it was also on the rise, strengthening to a near two-week peak of 4.1520 Norwegian crowns.
At 1115 GMT, mark/French franc was firm at 3.3730/35 and near session highs against 3.3698/3.3703 in late Europe on Tuesday.
Against the Swiss Franc, the mark was at 3.3724/26 after rising to a high of 82.30, its highest since July 31, and against 81.88/91 in late Europe.
Mark/lira was at 978.95/9.15 against 976.25/55. Against the Norwegian crown, the mark was trading at 4.1480/10 against 4.1080/4.1110 in late Europe.

"The Bundesbank report sounded the alarm bells...pointing to some inflationary risk with some focus on the currency as being a source of that," said Peter von Maydell, senior currency economist at UBS.

Traders on Wednesday cited talk of the Norwegian central bank intervening in the market to steady the crown. The currency has been extremely volatile as of late, rising to a three-month peak of 4.1180 on Monday as it drew some strength from firmer oil prices.
A spokesman for Norway's central bank, Norges Bank, however, declined to comment on the sudden slide in the currency on Wednesday and on whether it had intervened to stabilise it.
But traders were mainly preoccupied with Germany.
"The FX market has got very excited about the Buba report and German rates," said a senior trader at a French bank.

In its August monthly report on Wednesday, the Bundesbank warned the pace of consumer price increases had picked up in the last few months and that it would be steering its policy to ensure inflation remained under control. Traders said the report pushed dollar/mark down and mark crosses higher.
The report, which said the bank would observe forex movements closely and assess inflation risks, triggered dollar/mark and EMS/mark cross selling, said traders.
The central bank said: "The Bundesbank will orientate its policy in such a way that price stability, which has been essentially achieved, can be maintained."
It said it would observe foreign exchange movements closely and assess inflation risks.

The comments focused markets on money rates ahead of next week's repo tender, the conditions of which have not yet been announced. The Buba on Tuesday set this week's repo at an unchanged 3.0 percent, signalling monetary policy was on hold.
But analysts say the bank is intent on lifting the mark against the dollar in a bid to stem inflation.

"I think the Bundesbank is in a bit of a mess...They would really like to see the mark a bit stronger because that would impact on inflation," said Elizabeth Legge, economist at Bankgesellschaft Berlin.
But Legge said a rate hike in the short-term is unlikely as the Buba feels the recovery in Germany's economy is patchy.
"They would like, if they could, to talk the deutschmark up rather than make a change in their own monetary plans. I don't think they really, furiously, want to tighten yet," said Legge.
-- Julia Meehan, London newsroom +44 171 542 6701
